text:
maria: CI alert — perf/unit microbench failed on pr-13579, kv cache throughput down ~18% and p95 up ~60%. link: https://ci.redwood.dev/13579/results
ci-bot: [CI] perf/unit-test-microbench FAILED on pr-13579 — threshold diff exceeded (runners/kv_lookup). See artifacts: https://ci.redwood.dev/13579/artifacts
jake: copying the CI runner command: `./bazelisk run //bench:kv_lookup -- --runs=200` starting a local reproduce now
maria: attaching quick flamegraph from the CI artifact — big orange block in `slab::spill_to_slow_path` and a few syscalls for large allocs
olivia: oh neat. pr-13579 touched runtime/memory/small_slab.rs — changed bucket boundary rounding + growth factor. could be making more items hit the slow spill path
jake: confirm: reproduced on my A100 local, same bench: p95 regressed. `perf top` shows high time in `allocator::slow_alloc` and `memcpy`
kevin: can you paste the exact commit?
jake: commit 0a1b2c751f9d9e3b changed bucket growth from 1.5 -> 2.0 and removed an early-return in put_small()
maria: ok start a bisect? if it's that commit we should consider holding the canary rollout
jake: started git bisect; bad: HEAD (pr-13579), good: v2.4.2. bisect points to 0a1b2c751f9d9e3b as first bad
olivia: that aligns with the code change, interesting that microbench picks it up — maybe the microbench allocation size distribution sits right on the previous boundary so it now crosses into larger bucket causing spill
kevin: quick mitigation: cap the growth factor back to 1.5 and add a metric `kvcache_bucket_spill_count` so we can alert early. cheap patch, low risk
maria: can you open a PR with the cap + metric and unit test that simulates boundary? we should run CI perf before merging
jake: PR opened: #13601 — includes cap, a synthetic unit test that fills slab buckets, and a metric export. local bench shows p95 back to baseline
ci-bot: [CI] perf checks queued for pr-13601 — running microbench suite
maria: also hold the rollout for the canary group until we have green CI on the fix and 24h stable telemetry
oncall-bot: @kevin flagged the canary rollout for hold — tag: rollout/hold (expires in 2h)
kevin: adding dashboard alert for `kvcache_bucket_spill_rate` and an oncall runbook note. if rate > 0.5% fire page and rollback
olivia: followup: we should add a regression unit that varies allocation sizes across boundary to catch this in premerge checks
maria: agreed. summary: root cause = slab bucket boundary/growth change causing increased bucket spills into slow path -> extra allocations/copies -> higher p95. plan = land cap + metric (PR #13601) -> run perf CI -> merge if green -> monitor metric -> add targeted regression unit test. thanks all :thumbsup:
